investigacion.base:
Need week 41 (published ~Oct 16) and maybe week 42.I couldn't open the JIHS IDWR rapid-data page or the JIHS dashboard directly. The figures below come from news and prefectural reports that cite the health ministry (MHLW) and JIHS releases. The latest national value is **12.81 for week 41 (Oct 5–11)**, up for the second week in a row. The week the question asks about hasn't happened yet, so there's nothing to resolve against.

**⚠️ The question mixes up its week numbers.** In Japan's numbering for 2026, week 41 is Oct 5–11. That makes **week 43 = Oct 19–25** and **week 44 = Oct 26–Nov 1**. "The week ending Oct 25" and "published around Oct 30" both fit week 43, but the text says week 44. It's worth checking which one the question writer will actually use. A rising epidemic could make the two weeks' numbers quite different.

**National numbers so far in 2026 (MHLW/JIHS)**
- Week 30: 0.24. Week 34 (Aug 17–23): 1.11, above the 1.00 epidemic threshold. This was the 2nd-earliest epidemic onset since 1999, after 2009.
- Week 35: 1.76. Week 36: 3.29. Week 37: 5.54. Week 38: 8.48. Week 39: 7.17 (26,678 cases), about 7 times the 1.04 a year earlier. The dip in week 39 likely reflects the Silver Week holidays (my inference).
- Week 40 (Sep 28–Oct 4): 11.35, with 42,320 cases from about 3,700 sentinel sites.
- Week 41 (Oct 5–11), released Oct 16: 47,746 cases, 12.81 per sentinel, up from 11.35. That's a weekly growth of only about 13%, compared with +58% the week before.

**What's driving it in different regions**
- Okinawa is falling. It peaked at 42.50 in week 39 and has dropped two weeks running; Aichi has dropped three weeks running, to 11.47 in week 41.
- The Kanto region and Hokkaido are rising. In week 41 Kanagawa was at 21.60, Saitama 20.99, Chiba 19.55 and Hokkaido 16.21. 29 prefectures were above the advisory level of 10.
- School closures in week 41 covered 1,703 facilities, about 1.8 times the previous week's 937.
- Saga prefecture (A type dominant) rose from 5.42 to 7.63 in week 41.
- Kochi rose from 6.54 to 7.28.
- Separately, the acute respiratory infection (ARI) sentinel average for week 41 was 69.78, up for a second week (reported Oct 20).

**Upcoming releases**
- Week 42 (Oct 12–18): about Fri Oct 23. Oct 12 was the Sports Day holiday, which may hold this week's number down slightly.
- Week 43: about Oct 30.
- Week 44: about Nov 6.

**Base rates and context**
- Alert thresholds: 1.0 means the epidemic has started, 10 is the advisory level and 30 is the warning level.
- Last year's comparable figures were 0.80 in week 38 and 1.04 in week 39. From memory and not checked here, the 2025 season climbed sharply through October to roughly 14.9 in week 44. That may be where the question's "14.90" example comes from.
- For 2026, simple extrapolation from 12.81 gives a rough range of about 12 to 20 for weeks 43–44. Weekly growth has been anywhere from about 13% to 58%, and the falling southern prefectures are partly offsetting the rising eastern and northern ones.

**Prediction markets:** I didn't find any.

**Sources:**
- [1](https://c7service.co.jp/virus/influenza-national-outbreak-2026-september)
- [2](https://sugukuru-clinic.com/column/number-of-influenza-infections/)
- [3](https://resemom.jp/article/2026/10/16/87922.html)
- [4](https://news.yahoo.co.jp/articles/6ee2f77670a389d07be0ef043c57445dfb10d20d)

criterios: This question resolves to the national average number of reported influenza cases per sentinel medical institution (定点当たり報告数) for epidemiological week 44 of 2026 (the week ending Sunday, October 25, 2026), as published by Japan's Institute for Health Security (JIHS) in the Infectious Diseases Weekly Report (IDWR). The figure is the single nationwide "cases per sentinel" value for influenza, expected to be published on or around Friday, October 30, 2026, in the week-44 surveillance data table at https://id-info.jihs.go.jp/en/surveillance/idwr/rapid/2026/index.html . For example, a reported national average of 14.90 cases per sentinel resolves as 14.90. If the figure is also available via the JIHS dashboard at https://www.jihs.go.jp/content10/030/en_Dashboard.html or reported by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions), those may be used.
letra_pequena: If JIHS publishes a provisional week-44 value that is later revised, the first published national value for week 44 is used. If the week-44 figure is not published by any source by November 15, 2026, the question is annulled. Prefecture-level figures and hospital-based surveillance figures do not count; only the single nationwide per-sentinel average for influenza is used.
razonamientos:
(a) **Time left:** The week ending October 25 is five days away; its national figure is expected around October 30, in about ten days.

(b) **If nothing changed:** The average would remain **12.81 cases/sentinel**.

(c) **If the latest trend continued:** Repeating the most recent weekly increase of about 13% for two weeks would put it near **16.4 cases/sentinel**.

(d) **Experts and markets:** The cited surveillance reports show growth nationally but declines in some prefectures. I have no quantified expert forecast or prediction-market estimate to rely on.

(e) **Unexpected low outcome:** A broad decline, compounded by holiday-related reporting effects, could bring the reading below 10.

(f) **Unexpected high outcome:** Rapid spread across the rising eastern and northern regions could push it above 30.

**Week-number caveat:** October 19–25 appears to be epidemiological **week 43**, not week 44. I forecast the explicitly specified *week ending October 25*, consistent with the stated October 30 publication date.

**(a) Time until the outcome is known.** The week ending Oct 25, 2026 is ISO week 43, published around Fri Oct 30. That is about 10 days away. If the resolver instead uses the week-44 table, it would be published around Nov 6, about 17 days away. Two of the question's three descriptors (the end date and the publication date) point to week 43, so I put most weight there. I keep some weight on week 44, which would probably be somewhat higher.

**(b) If nothing changed.** The value would stay around 12.8.

**(c) If the current trend continued.** The growth rate fell from +58% to +13%, partly because Okinawa and Aichi are declining. Week 42 is likely held down by the Oct 12 Sports Day holiday, perhaps to 13–14. After that, continued 10–20% weekly growth gives:
- Week 43: about 15–18.
- Week 44: about 17–21.

Several signals point to further growth:
- Kanto (Kanagawa 21.6, Saitama 21.0, Chiba 19.6) and Hokkaido are rising.
- Kanto carries a large share of all sentinel sites.
- School closures rose 1.8 times in a week.

**(d) Experts and markets.** I found no markets. Commentary describes the season as expanding, with 29 prefectures above the advisory level. Last season, growth accelerated sharply through late October and November.

**(e) Low scenario.** The epidemic peaks early: the south keeps falling, Kanto plateaus, and holiday or reporting effects suppress counts. The national figure then falls to 10–12.

**(f) High scenario.** Kanto, Kansai and the north accelerate together, or a new subtype wave starts, as in the steep 2025 November climb. With the week-44 interpretation, the value could reach 25–30.

(a) **Time left:** About 10 days until the expected October 30 publication.  
(b) **If nothing changed:** The national average would remain 12.81 cases/sentinel.  
(c) **If the latest weekly trend continued:** Repeating the roughly 13% increase for two weeks would produce about 16.3 cases/sentinel.  
(d) **Experts and markets:** The surveillance reports establish the recent readings, but I have no reliable expert numerical forecast or liquid market forecast for October 25.  
(e) **Unexpected low scenario:** Declines spread beyond Okinawa and offset growth elsewhere, bringing the average toward 10.  
(f) **Unexpected high scenario:** Transmission accelerates across eastern and northern Japan, pushing the average toward 30.
